jer-24-6-7: God promises the exiles in Babylon to watch over them for good, bring them home and give them a heart to know Him, for they will return to Him wholeheartedly.
jer-29-10-11: God promises the exiles in Babylon that after seventy years He will bring them home, for His plans for them are for peace and a hopeful future, not harm.
jer-29-12-14: God promises the exiles that when they seek Him with all their heart they will find Him, and He will restore their fortunes and gather them home.
jer-30-8-10: God promises to break the yoke of oppression from Jacob's neck; they will serve Him and a king from David's line, and return from captivity in peace.
jer-30-17: God promises to restore Zion's health and heal her wounds, because others called her an outcast no one cared for.
jer-30-18-22: God promises to restore Jacob's homes and rebuild Jerusalem, filling it with thanksgiving and growth; they will be His people and He their God.
jer-31-3: God tells Israel He has loved them with an everlasting love and has drawn them with loving kindness.
jer-31-8-9: God promises to bring His people home from the far north, including the blind, lame and pregnant, leading them by streams as a father to Israel.
jer-31-12-14: God promises the returning exiles joy on Zion, abundant grain, wine and flocks, souls like a watered garden, and mourning turned into gladness.
jer-31-16-17: God tells weeping Rachel to stop her tears, for her children will return from the enemy's land; there is hope for her future.
jer-31-20: God calls Ephraim His dear son; though He speaks against him, His heart yearns for him and He will surely have mercy on him.
jer-31-25: God promises to refresh the weary and satisfy every sorrowful soul as He restores His people.
jer-31-31-34: God promises Israel and Judah a new covenant: He will write His law on their hearts, all will know Him, and He will forgive their sin. Hebrews says Jesus brings this covenant.
jer-32-17: God made heaven and earth by His great power, and nothing is too hard for Him, as Jeremiah confesses during the siege.
jer-32-27: God is the LORD of all flesh, and nothing is too hard for Him, including bringing His people back to the land.
jer-32-37-41: God promises to gather His people from exile, give them one heart to fear Him and make an everlasting covenant, rejoicing to do them good in the land.
jer-33-3: God invites the imprisoned Jeremiah to call on Him, promising to answer and show him great hidden things about Jerusalem's restoration.
jer-33-6-9: God promises to heal Jerusalem, restore Judah and Israel, cleanse and forgive all their sins, and make the city a name of joy before the nations.
jer-33-10-11: God promises that the desolate streets of Jerusalem will again hear joy, weddings and thanksgiving in His house, as He restores the land.
jer-33-14-16: God promises to fulfill His good word by raising a righteous Branch for David who will do justice; Judah will be saved and Jerusalem dwell safely.
jer-33-20-22: God declares His covenant with David and the Levites as unbreakable as day and night, and promises to multiply their descendants beyond counting.
jer-39-17-18: God promises Ebed-Melech, who rescued Jeremiah, that he will escape with his life when Jerusalem falls, because he trusted in the LORD.
jer-42-10-12: God promises Judah's survivors that if they stay in the land rather than flee to Egypt, He will build them up and save them from Babylon.
jer-46-27-28: God tells Jacob not to fear, promising to bring them back from captivity; He will discipline them justly but never make a full end of them.
jer-50-4-5: God foretells that Israel and Judah will return together, weeping as they seek Him, and join themselves to Him in an everlasting covenant.
jer-50-19-20: God promises to restore Israel to its pastures and pardon the remnant He spares, so that no guilt will be found in them.
lam-3-21-23: God's loving kindness keeps us from being consumed, even amid Jerusalem's ruin; His mercies never fail and are new every morning; great is His faithfulness.
lam-3-24-26: God is the portion of those who hope in Him; He is good to those who wait for Him, and it is good to wait quietly for His salvation.
lam-3-31-33: God will not cast off forever; though He brings grief, He will show compassion, for He does not willingly afflict anyone.
lam-3-55-58: God heard the cry from the depths of the pit, came near and said, "Don't be afraid," taking up the case and redeeming the life of the one who called.
ezk-11-19-20: God promises the exiles one heart and a new spirit, replacing their stony heart with a heart of flesh so they will walk in His ways and be His people.
ezk-16-60-63: God promises unfaithful Jerusalem that He will remember His covenant and establish an everlasting one, forgiving all she has done.
ezk-18-21-23: God promises that if the wicked turn from all their sins and do what is right, they will live and their past offenses will not be remembered, for He takes no pleasure in their death.
ezk-18-30-32: God will judge Israel each by their ways, so He pleads with them to repent and get a new heart and spirit, for He takes no pleasure in anyone's death: turn and live.
ezk-20-41-44: God promises to gather Israel from the nations and accept them as a pleasing aroma, dealing with them for His name's sake rather than as their evil deserved.
ezk-28-25-26: God promises that when He gathers Israel from the nations, they will dwell securely in their land, build houses and plant vineyards.
ezk-34-11-12: God promises that He Himself will search for His scattered sheep and rescue them from wherever they were scattered on a dark day.
ezk-34-13-15: God promises to bring His flock home, feed them on good pasture on Israel's mountains and be their shepherd, making them lie down in safety.
ezk-34-16: God promises to seek the lost, bring back the strays, bind up the injured and strengthen the weak, while judging those who exploited the flock.
ezk-34-22-24: God promises to rescue His flock and set over them one shepherd, His servant David, with the LORD as their God. Christians see this fulfilled in Jesus, the Good Shepherd.
ezk-34-25-26: God promises His restored people a covenant of peace, safety from wild beasts and showers of blessing in their season.
ezk-34-27-28: God promises that the land will yield its crops, and when He breaks Israel's yoke they will live securely, no longer plundered or afraid.
ezk-34-30-31: God promises Israel they will know He is with them; they are the sheep of His pasture, and He is their God.
ezk-36-9-11: God promises the mountains of Israel that He is for them; the land will be farmed again, its towns rebuilt and filled, and He will do more good than before.
ezk-36-24-25: God promises to gather Israel from all nations, bring them home and sprinkle clean water on them, cleansing them from all impurity and idols.
ezk-36-26-28: God promises Israel a new heart and a new spirit, replacing the heart of stone with flesh, and to put His Spirit within them so they walk in His ways.
ezk-36-29-30: God promises to save Israel from all uncleanness and make grain and fruit abundant, so they will no longer suffer the disgrace of famine.
ezk-36-33-36: God promises that when He cleanses Israel from sin, their ruined cities will be rebuilt and the desolate land become like Eden, so the nations will know He did it.
ezk-37-5-6: God promises the dry bones that He will give them sinews, flesh and breath so they will live, a picture of exiled Israel restored to life.
ezk-37-12-14: God promises the exiles, who felt dead and hopeless, to open their graves, put His Spirit in them so they live and settle them in their own land.
ezk-37-21-23: God promises to gather Israel from the nations into one nation under one king, cleansing them from idols, so they will be His people and He their God.
ezk-37-24-27: God promises His servant David as Israel's one shepherd-king, an everlasting covenant of peace and His sanctuary among them forever. Christians see this fulfilled in Christ.
ezk-39-25-29: God promises to restore Jacob and have mercy on all Israel, bringing them home in safety and never again hiding His face, for He has poured out His Spirit on them.
ezk-47-8-9: God shows Ezekiel a river flowing from the temple that heals the Dead Sea, so that life swarms wherever it goes.
ezk-47-12: God shows Ezekiel fruit trees along the temple river, bearing fruit every month with leaves for healing, a picture Revelation 22 takes up.
dan-2-20-22: God owns wisdom and might; He changes times and seasons, removes and sets up kings, gives wisdom to the wise and reveals deep and hidden things.
dan-2-44: God will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed; it will break all earthly kingdoms and stand forever.
dan-3-17-18: God is able to deliver from the furnace, the three young men tell the king; but even if He does not, they will not worship his gods.
dan-3-24-25: God protected the three men in the furnace, where Nebuchadnezzar saw four men walking unharmed, the fourth like a son of the gods.
dan-4-34-35: God's dominion is everlasting and no one can stop His hand or question Him, as the humbled Nebuchadnezzar confesses when his reason returns.
dan-6-22: God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths, Daniel tells the king, because he was found innocent before Him.
dan-6-26-27: God is the living God, enduring forever, whose kingdom will not be destroyed; He rescues and works wonders, as He did for Daniel.
dan-7-13-14: God gives one like a son of man, coming with the clouds, an everlasting kingdom over all peoples; Jesus took the title Son of Man from this vision.
dan-7-18: God promises that the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever.
dan-7-27: God promises that the kingdom and dominion under the whole sky will be given to the saints of the Most High; His kingdom is everlasting and all rulers will obey Him.
dan-9-9: God, the Lord, is merciful and forgiving, even though His people have rebelled against Him.
dan-9-18-19: God is asked to hear, forgive and act for ruined Jerusalem, not because of Israel's righteousness but for His great mercy and His own name.
dan-10-12: God heard Daniel's prayer from the first day he humbled himself to seek understanding, and an angel came in response.
dan-10-18-19: God's messenger touched Daniel, called him greatly beloved, and told him to have peace and be strong, and Daniel was strengthened.
dan-12-1: God promises that in a time of unequaled distress His people, everyone written in the book, will be delivered.
dan-12-2-3: God reveals that many who sleep in the dust will awake, some to everlasting life and some to everlasting shame; the wise will shine like the stars forever.
dan-12-13: God promises Daniel that he will rest and then rise to receive his inheritance at the end of the days.
hos-1-10: God promises that Israel, once called "Not my people," will become countless and be called "sons of the living God." Paul applies this to God's calling of Gentiles too.
hos-2-14-15: God promises to lead unfaithful Israel into the wilderness, speak tenderly to her and make the Valley of Trouble a door of hope.
hos-2-16-20: God promises Israel that she will call Him "my husband," forget the Baals and be betrothed to Him forever in righteousness, love, compassion and faithfulness.
hos-2-21-23: God promises to answer with rain and harvest, show mercy to the one called unloved and say to "Not my people," "You are my people."
hos-6-1-3: God's people urge one another to return to the LORD, who has wounded them and will heal them; the following verses show their repentance was shallow.
hos-11-1: God loved Israel as a child and called His son out of Egypt; Matthew sees this pattern fulfilled when Jesus returned from Egypt.
hos-11-3-4: God taught Israel to walk, held them by the arms, healed them and led them with cords of love, bending down to feed them.
hos-11-8-9: God cannot give up Israel; His compassion is stirred, and because He is God and not man, He will not destroy them in fierce anger.
hos-14-4-5: God promises returning Israel to heal their waywardness and love them freely; He will be like dew, and they will blossom like the lily.
hos-14-7: God promises that restored Israel will flourish like grain and vine and offer shade to others.
jol-2-12-13: God calls Judah to return to Him with all their heart, tearing their hearts and not their garments, for He is gracious, merciful and slow to anger.
jol-2-18-19: God took pity on His people and promised to send grain, wine and oil to satisfy them and end their disgrace among the nations.
jol-2-21-22: God tells the scorched land and animals not to fear, for He has done great things; pastures will turn green and trees will bear fruit again.
jol-2-23-24: God promises Zion the early and latter rain as before, so their threshing floors will be full and their vats overflow.
jol-2-25-27: God promises Judah to restore the years the locusts ate; they will eat their fill, praise Him and know He is among Israel.
jol-2-28-29: God promises to pour out His Spirit on all flesh, sons and daughters, old and young, even servants; Peter declares this began at Pentecost.
jol-2-32: God promises that everyone who calls on the LORD's name will be saved, words Paul applies to all who call on Jesus.
jol-3-16-17: God will roar from Zion in judgment, yet He will be a refuge and stronghold for His people, dwelling among them in holy Jerusalem.
jol-3-18: God promises a coming day of abundance, with mountains dripping wine and a fountain flowing from His house to water the dry valleys.
amo-5-4: God tells Israel, "Seek me, and you will live," rather than trusting empty worship at their shrines.
amo-5-14-15: God calls Israel to seek good, hate evil and establish justice, so they may live; perhaps He will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.
amo-9-11-12: God promises to raise up David's fallen tent and rebuild its ruins; James saw this fulfilled as Gentiles turned to God.
amo-9-13-15: God promises to bring Israel back from captivity, with harvests so abundant they overlap, and to plant them in their land never to be uprooted.
oba-1-15-17: God warns Edom that the day of the LORD is near and their deeds will return on them, but on Mount Zion there will be deliverance and holiness.
oba-1-21: God promises that deliverers will go up on Mount Zion to judge Edom, and the kingdom will be the LORD's.
jon-2-1-2: God answered Jonah when he called from the belly of the fish in his distress, hearing him even from the depths.
jon-2-6-7: God brought Jonah's life up from the pit when he remembered the LORD as his life was fainting away.
jon-2-8-9: God alone gives salvation; those who cling to idols forsake His mercy, while Jonah vows thanksgiving.
jon-3-9-10: God saw Nineveh turn from its evil ways and relented from the disaster He had announced.
jon-4-2: God is gracious, merciful, slow to anger and abundant in loving kindness, ready to relent, which is why Jonah fled from showing mercy to Israel's enemies.
mic-4-1-3: God promises that in the latter days the nations will stream to His mountain to learn His ways; He will judge between them, and they will beat swords into plowshares.
mic-4-4: God promises a coming peace in which everyone will sit under his own vine and fig tree, with no one to make them afraid.
mic-4-5: God's people will walk in the name of the LORD their God forever, though the nations follow their own gods.
mic-5-2: God promises a ruler for Israel from little Bethlehem, whose origins are from ancient times; Matthew records Jesus' birth there as its fulfillment.
mic-5-4-5: God's promised ruler will shepherd His people in the LORD's strength; His greatness will reach the ends of the earth, and He will be their peace.
mic-6-8: God has shown what is good and what He requires: to act justly, love mercy and walk humbly with Him.
mic-7-7-8: God will hear Micah as he waits for Him; though he falls he will rise, and when he sits in darkness the LORD will be his light.
mic-7-9: God will take up Israel's case after they bear His anger for their sin, bringing them out to the light to see His righteousness.
mic-7-18-19: God pardons iniquity and does not stay angry forever, for He delights in loving kindness; He will tread our sins underfoot and cast them into the depths of the sea.
mic-7-20: God will show faithfulness to Jacob and loving kindness to Abraham, as He swore to their fathers long ago.
nam-1-7: God is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble, and He knows those who take refuge in Him.
hab-2-3: God tells Habakkuk that the vision awaits its appointed time; though it seems slow, it will surely come and not delay.
hab-2-4: God contrasts the proud with the righteous, who will live by faith; Paul and Hebrews quote this to show we are made right with God through faith.
hab-2-14: God promises that the earth will be filled with the knowledge of His glory as the waters cover the sea.
hab-3-17-19: God remains Habakkuk's joy and strength even if every crop and flock fails; He makes his feet like a deer's on the heights.
zep-3-9-10: God promises to purify the lips of the peoples so all may call on His name and serve Him together, with worshipers coming even from Cush.
zep-3-11-12: God promises to remove the proud from Jerusalem, leaving a humble and lowly people who take refuge in His name.
zep-3-13: God promises that the remnant of Israel will do no wrong and speak no lies, and will rest like a flock with no one to make them afraid.
zep-3-14-15: God has taken away Jerusalem's judgment and cast out her enemy; the LORD, Israel's King, is in her midst, so she need fear no evil.
zep-3-16-17: God tells Zion not to fear, for He is among her as a mighty Savior; He will rejoice over her with joy, quiet her with His love and sing over her.
zep-3-19-20: God promises to deal with Israel's oppressors, save the lame, gather the scattered and turn their shame into honor among all peoples.
hag-1-13: God told the returned exiles, as they obeyed and began rebuilding the temple, "I am with you."
hag-2-4-5: God tells Zerubbabel, Joshua and the people to be strong and work on the temple, for He is with them as He covenanted at the exodus, and His Spirit remains among them.
hag-2-6-9: God promises to shake the nations and fill the rebuilt temple with glory greater than the former, and in that place to give peace.
hag-2-19: God promises the returned exiles, 'From today I will bless you,' even though their vines and fruit trees have not yet produced a harvest.
hag-2-23: God promises Zerubbabel, David's heir, to make him like a signet ring, for He has chosen him.
zec-1-3: God tells His people, "Return to me, and I will return to you."
zec-1-16-17: God has returned to Jerusalem with mercy; His house will be rebuilt, His cities will overflow with prosperity, and He will again comfort Zion.
zec-2-4-5: God promises that Jerusalem will overflow beyond its walls, and He Himself will be a wall of fire around it and the glory within it.
zec-2-8-9: God declares that whoever touches His people touches the apple of His eye, and He will raise His hand against the nations that plundered them.
zec-2-10-11: God calls Zion to sing, for He is coming to dwell among her, and many nations will join themselves to Him and become His people.
zec-3-4-5: God removes Joshua the high priest's filthy garments, takes away his iniquity and clothes him in clean garments.
zec-3-8-9: God promises to bring His servant the Branch and remove the iniquity of the land in a single day.
zec-4-6: God tells Zerubbabel the temple will be rebuilt "not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit."
zec-8-3-4: God promises to return to Zion and dwell in Jerusalem, the City of Truth, where old men and women will again sit in its streets.
zec-8-7-8: God promises to save His people from east and west and bring them to Jerusalem; they will be His people and He their God in truth and righteousness.
zec-8-12-13: God promises the remnant that crops, vines and dew will yield their increase, and Judah and Israel, once a curse, will become a blessing.
zec-8-16-17: God tells His restored people to speak truth, judge justly, plot no evil against neighbors and love no false oath, for He hates these things.
zec-9-9-10: God promises Jerusalem her righteous King, coming humbly on a donkey with salvation and speaking peace to the nations; the Gospels show Jesus fulfilling this.
zec-9-11-12: God promises, by the blood of His covenant, to free His captive people and calls these prisoners of hope to return, restoring double to them.
zec-10-1: God, who makes the storm clouds, is the one to ask for spring rain, and He gives showers for everyone's fields.
zec-10-6: God promises to strengthen Judah and save Joseph, bringing them back in mercy as though He had never cast them off, for He will answer them.
zec-12-1: God, who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth and forms the human spirit, speaks this word concerning Israel.
zec-12-10: God promises to pour a spirit of grace and supplication on Jerusalem; they will look on the one they pierced and mourn. John applies this to Jesus' crucifixion.
zec-13-1: God promises that a fountain will be opened for David's house and Jerusalem to cleanse them from sin and impurity.
zec-13-9: God will refine a remnant like silver and gold; they will call on His name and He will answer, "They are my people," and they will say, "The LORD is my God."
zec-14-8-9: God promises living waters flowing from Jerusalem all year, and the LORD will be King over all the earth, one LORD with one name.
mal-1-2: God tells His doubting people, "I have loved you," pointing to His choice of Jacob as proof.
mal-3-1: God promises to send His messenger to prepare His way, and then the Lord will suddenly come to His temple; the Gospels identify the messenger as John the Baptist preparing for Jesus.
mal-3-6: God does not change, and that is why Jacob's unfaithful descendants have not been consumed.
mal-3-7: God tells Israel, who turned from His ordinances, "Return to me, and I will return to you."
mal-3-10-11: God tells Judah to bring the whole tithe into His storehouse and test Him, promising to open heaven's windows in blessing and rebuke the devourer of their crops.
mal-3-16-17: God heard those who feared Him and recorded them in a book of remembrance; He promises they will be His treasured possession, spared as a father spares his son.
mal-4-2: God promises that for those who fear His name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings, and they will leap like calves from the stall.
mat-1-21-23: God promised Joseph that Mary's son would be named Jesus because He would save His people from their sins, fulfilling Isaiah's sign of Immanuel, "God with us."
mat-4-4: Jesus answers temptation with Scripture: people do not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from God's mouth.
mat-5-3-10: Jesus promises God's blessing to the poor in spirit, the mourning, the gentle, the hungry for righteousness, the merciful, the pure in heart, peacemakers and the persecuted: comfort, mercy, seeing God and the Kingdom.
mat-5-11-12: Jesus promises those insulted and persecuted falsely for His sake a great reward in heaven, so they can rejoice, as the prophets were treated the same way.
mat-6-6: Jesus teaches to pray to the Father in secret, promising that the Father who sees in secret will reward you.
mat-6-8: Jesus teaches that the Father knows what we need before we ask Him, so prayer need not be empty repetition.
mat-6-9-13: Jesus teaches His disciples to pray to the Father for His name to be honored, His Kingdom and will to come, daily bread, forgiveness and deliverance from the evil one.
mat-6-14-15: Jesus teaches that the Father will forgive those who forgive others, but will not forgive those who refuse to forgive.
mat-6-25-26: Jesus tells His followers not to worry about food or clothing, for the Father feeds the birds and they are worth far more.
mat-6-27-30: Jesus says worry adds nothing to life; if God so clothes the short-lived grass of the field, He will much more clothe His people.
mat-6-31-34: Jesus promises that the Father knows what His people need, and if they seek first His Kingdom and righteousness, these things will be given as well, so they need not worry about tomorrow.
mat-7-7-8: Jesus promises that those who ask will receive, those who seek will find, and to those who knock the door will be opened.
mat-7-9-11: Jesus says that if human parents give good gifts to their children, the Father in heaven will give good things to those who ask Him all the more.
mat-7-24-25: Jesus teaches that whoever hears His words and does them is like a wise man who built on rock; when storms came, the house stood.
mat-8-2-3: Jesus, willing to heal, touched a leper who asked to be made clean, and he was cleansed immediately.
mat-8-16-17: Jesus drove out spirits with a word and healed all the sick brought to Him, fulfilling Isaiah: "He took our infirmities and bore our diseases."
mat-9-2: Jesus saw the faith of those who brought a paralyzed man and told him, "Cheer up! Your sins are forgiven."
mat-9-12-13: Jesus came to call sinners to repentance, as a doctor comes for the sick, and God desires mercy rather than sacrifice.
mat-9-21-22: Jesus told the woman who touched His garment in faith, "Daughter, cheer up! Your faith has made you well," and she was healed.
mat-9-36-38: Jesus had compassion on the crowds, harassed like sheep without a shepherd, and told His disciples to pray for the Lord of the harvest to send workers.
mat-10-19-20: Jesus promises His disciples that when they are handed over to authorities, the Spirit of the Father will give them what to say.
mat-10-28-31: Jesus tells His disciples not to fear those who can kill only the body, for not a sparrow falls without the Father, and every hair of their heads is numbered.
mat-10-32: Jesus promises that everyone who acknowledges Him before others, He will acknowledge before His Father in heaven.
mat-10-39: Jesus teaches that whoever clings to his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for Jesus' sake will find it.
mat-10-42: Jesus promises that whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of His little ones because he is a disciple will not lose his reward.
mat-11-28-30: Jesus promises rest to all who are weary and burdened and come to Him; He is gentle and humble, His yoke is easy and His burden light.
mat-12-18-21: God's chosen servant, on whom He puts His Spirit, will gently bring justice to victory without breaking a bruised reed; Matthew says Jesus fulfills this, and in His name the nations will hope.
mat-12-31: Jesus teaches that every sin and blasphemy can be forgiven, but blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
mat-13-43: Jesus promises that at the end of the age the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father's Kingdom.
mat-14-27: Jesus came to His frightened disciples on the water and said, "Cheer up! It is I! Don't be afraid."
mat-16-18-19: Jesus promises to build His church on this rock, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it; He gives Peter the keys of the Kingdom.
mat-16-24-25: Jesus calls anyone who would follow Him to deny himself and take up his cross; whoever loses his life for His sake will find it.
mat-17-5: God the Father spoke from the cloud at the transfiguration: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him."
mat-18-3-4: Jesus teaches that unless people turn and become like little children they will not enter the Kingdom, and the humble are greatest there.
mat-18-10: Jesus warns against despising little ones, for their angels in heaven always see the face of His Father.
mat-18-12-14: Jesus teaches that like a shepherd who seeks one lost sheep, the Father does not want any of these little ones to perish.
mat-18-19-20: Jesus promises that when two agree in prayer the Father will act, and where two or three gather in His name, He is there among them.
mat-19-14: Jesus welcomes little children, saying the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to such as these.
mat-19-26: Jesus says salvation is impossible for people, but with God all things are possible.
mat-19-28-29: Jesus promises the Twelve thrones in the renewal of all things, and everyone who has left home or family for His sake a hundredfold reward and eternal life.
mat-20-26-28: Jesus teaches that greatness among His followers means serving, just as He came not to be served but to serve and give His life as a ransom for many.
mat-21-21-22: Jesus tells His disciples that faith without doubt could move a mountain, and whatever they ask in prayer believing, they will receive.
mat-24-13: Jesus promises that whoever endures to the end will be saved.
mat-24-30-31: Jesus promises that He will come on the clouds with power and great glory and send His angels to gather His chosen ones from the four winds.
mat-24-35: Jesus declares that heaven and earth will pass away, but His words will never pass away.
mat-25-21: In Jesus' parable, the master tells the faithful servant, "Well done," setting him over much and inviting him into his joy.
mat-25-34: Jesus says the King will welcome those blessed by the Father to inherit the Kingdom prepared for them from the foundation of the world.
mat-25-40: Jesus teaches that whatever is done for the least of His brothers is done for Him.
mat-26-26-28: Jesus gave His disciples the bread as His body and the cup as His blood of the new covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
mat-28-5-7: God's angel told the women not to fear: Jesus, who was crucified, has risen as He said and is going ahead of His disciples to Galilee.
mat-28-18-20: Jesus, given all authority, sends His disciples to make disciples of all nations, promising, "I am with you always, even to the end of the age."
mrk-1-14-15: Jesus proclaimed that the time is fulfilled and God's Kingdom is near, calling people to repent and believe the Good News.
mrk-2-5: Jesus saw the faith of the paralyzed man's friends and told him, "Son, your sins are forgiven you."
mrk-2-17: Jesus came to call sinners, not the righteous, as a doctor comes for the sick.
mrk-4-39-40: Jesus rebuked the wind and calmed the sea with a word, then asked His frightened disciples why they had no faith.
mrk-5-34: Jesus told the woman healed by touching Him, "Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace."
mrk-5-36: Jesus told Jairus, after hearing his daughter had died, "Don't be afraid, only believe."
mrk-6-50: Jesus came to His terrified disciples on the water and said, "Cheer up! It is I! Don't be afraid."
mrk-8-34-35: Jesus calls whoever would follow Him to deny himself and take up his cross; whoever loses his life for Him and the Good News will save it.
mrk-9-23: Jesus tells the father of a suffering boy, "All things are possible to him who believes."
mrk-10-14-15: Jesus welcomes little children, for God's Kingdom belongs to such as these, and whoever does not receive it like a child will not enter it.
mrk-10-27: Jesus says salvation is impossible for people, but not for God, for all things are possible with God.
mrk-10-29-30: Jesus promises those who leave home and family for Him and the Good News a hundred times more now, with persecutions, and eternal life in the age to come.
mrk-10-45: Jesus came not to be served but to serve and to give His life as a ransom for many.
mrk-11-24: Jesus tells His disciples that whatever they ask in prayer, believing they have received it, they will have.
mrk-13-11: Jesus promises His disciples that when arrested they need not worry what to say, for the Holy Spirit will speak through them.
mrk-13-13: Jesus warns His followers they will be hated for His name, but promises that whoever endures to the end will be saved.
mrk-13-26-27: Jesus promises that He will come in clouds with great power and glory and gather His chosen ones from the ends of the earth.
mrk-13-31: Jesus declares that heaven and earth will pass away, but His words will not pass away.
mrk-16-6-7: God's messenger told the women that Jesus, who was crucified, has risen and is going ahead of His disciples and Peter to Galilee.
luk-1-30-33: God tells Mary through Gabriel that she will bear a son named Jesus, the Son of the Most High, who will reign on David's throne forever.
luk-1-37: God's word never fails; nothing He has spoken is impossible.
luk-1-45: Blessed is Mary for believing, Elizabeth says, because what the Lord told her will be fulfilled.
luk-1-46-50: God the Savior looked on His humble servant Mary and did great things for her; His mercy reaches every generation of those who fear Him.
luk-1-52-55: God brings down rulers and lifts the lowly, fills the hungry and sends the rich away empty, and helps Israel, remembering His mercy to Abraham.
luk-1-68-75: God has visited and redeemed His people, raising up a savior from David's house to keep His covenant with Abraham, so they may serve Him without fear in holiness.
luk-1-76-79: God will send John ahead of the Lord to give knowledge of salvation through forgiveness, as His tender mercy brings the dawn from on high to those in darkness.
luk-2-10-11: God's angel announces good news of great joy for all the people: a Savior is born in David's city, Christ the Lord.
luk-2-14: God is given glory in the highest by the angels, who proclaim peace on earth to those He favors.
luk-2-29-32: God kept His word to Simeon, who saw His salvation in the infant Jesus, a light for the nations and glory for Israel.
luk-4-18-19: Jesus announces that the Spirit of the Lord has anointed Him to bring good news to the poor, release to captives, sight to the blind and freedom for the oppressed.
luk-5-12-13: Jesus, willing to heal, touched a man full of leprosy who begged to be made clean, and the leprosy left him immediately.
luk-5-20: Jesus saw the faith of those who brought a paralyzed man and told him, "Your sins are forgiven you."
luk-6-20-23: Jesus promises His disciples that the poor, hungry, weeping and persecuted for His sake are blessed: the Kingdom is theirs, they will be filled and laugh, and their reward in heaven is great.
luk-6-35-36: Jesus calls His followers to love enemies and lend expecting nothing, promising great reward as children of the Most High, who is kind to the ungrateful.
luk-6-37-38: Jesus teaches not to judge or condemn but to forgive and give, for the measure you use will be measured back to you, pressed down and running over.
luk-7-47-48: Jesus told the woman who loved much that her many sins were forgiven.
luk-8-48: Jesus told the woman healed by touching Him, "Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace."
luk-8-50: Jesus told Jairus, "Don't be afraid. Only believe, and she will be healed," before raising his daughter.
luk-9-23-24: Jesus calls anyone who would follow Him to deny himself and take up his cross daily; whoever loses his life for His sake will save it.
luk-10-19-20: Jesus gave the seventy-two authority over the enemy's power, but told them to rejoice most that their names are written in heaven.
luk-10-21: Jesus rejoices and thanks the Father for hiding these things from the wise and revealing them to little children, as pleased Him.
luk-10-22: Jesus says all things have been handed to Him by the Father; no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom He reveals Him.
luk-11-9-10: Jesus promises that everyone who keeps asking receives, who keeps seeking finds, and to the one who keeps knocking the door will be opened.
luk-11-11-13: Jesus promises that if earthly fathers give good gifts, the heavenly Father will much more give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him.
luk-12-6-7: Jesus tells His friends not to fear, for God does not forget a single sparrow and the hairs of their heads are all counted.
luk-12-8: Jesus promises that everyone who acknowledges Him before others, He will acknowledge before the angels of God.
luk-12-22-24: Jesus tells His disciples not to worry about food or clothing, for God feeds the ravens and they are worth far more.
luk-12-29-32: Jesus promises His little flock that the Father knows their needs, and as they seek His Kingdom these things will be added, for it is His pleasure to give them the Kingdom.
luk-12-33-34: Jesus teaches to give to the needy and store up treasure in heaven that never fails, for where your treasure is, your heart will be.
luk-13-29-30: Jesus says people will come from east, west, north and south to sit in God's Kingdom, where some who are last will be first.
luk-15-4-7: Jesus teaches that like a shepherd who finds his lost sheep, there is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine who need no repentance.
luk-15-8-10: Jesus teaches that like a woman who finds her lost coin, there is joy before God's angels over one sinner who repents.
luk-15-20-24: In Jesus' parable, the father runs to his returning son, embraces him and restores him with a feast, picturing God's welcome for the repentant.
luk-18-7-8: Jesus promises that God will bring justice for His chosen ones who cry to Him day and night, and asks whether the Son of Man will find faith when He comes.
luk-18-13-14: Jesus teaches that the tax collector who prayed, "God, be merciful to me, a sinner," went home justified, for the humble will be exalted.
luk-18-16-17: Jesus welcomes little children, for God's Kingdom belongs to such as these, and whoever does not receive it like a child will not enter it.
luk-18-27: Jesus says what is impossible with people is possible with God.
luk-18-29-30: Jesus promises that whoever leaves home or family for God's Kingdom will receive many times more in this age and eternal life in the age to come.
luk-19-9-10: Jesus declares salvation has come to Zacchaeus' house, for the Son of Man came to seek and save the lost.
luk-21-14-15: Jesus promises His disciples that when brought before authorities He will give them words and wisdom their opponents cannot resist.
luk-21-18-19: Jesus promises His persecuted disciples that not a hair of their heads will perish, and by their endurance they will gain their lives.
luk-21-27-28: Jesus promises He will come in a cloud with power and great glory, so when these things begin His followers should lift up their heads, for their redemption is near.
luk-21-33: Jesus declares that heaven and earth will pass away, but His words will never pass away.
luk-22-19-20: Jesus gave His disciples bread as His body given for them and the cup as the new covenant in His blood, telling them to do this in memory of Him.
luk-23-34: Jesus prays from the cross, "Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing."
luk-23-42-43: Jesus promises the repentant thief who asks to be remembered, "Today you will be with me in Paradise."
luk-24-5-7: God's messengers tell the women that Jesus is not among the dead but has risen, as He said He would on the third day.
luk-24-38-39: Jesus, risen, showed His troubled disciples His hands and feet, inviting them to touch Him and see that He is truly alive in body.
luk-24-46-49: Jesus explains that the Christ had to suffer and rise, so forgiveness is preached to all nations, and promises to send the Father's promise to clothe His witnesses with power.
jhn-1-12-13: God gives everyone who receives Jesus and believes in His name the right to become His children, born not of human will but of God.
jhn-1-14: God's eternal Word became flesh and lived among us, full of grace and truth, revealing the glory of the Father's only Son.
jhn-1-16-17: God has given us grace upon grace from Christ's fullness; the law came through Moses, but grace and truth through Jesus Christ.
jhn-1-29: God's Lamb, Jesus, takes away the sin of the world, as John the Baptist declares.
jhn-3-3-5: Jesus teaches that no one can see or enter God's Kingdom unless born anew of water and the Spirit.
jhn-3-14-15: Jesus says He must be lifted up like Moses' serpent, so that whoever believes in Him will have eternal life.
jhn-3-16-17: God so loved the world that He gave His only Son, so that whoever believes in Him will not perish but have eternal life; He sent Him to save, not condemn.
jhn-3-18: Jesus says whoever believes in God's Son is not condemned, but whoever does not believe is condemned already.
jhn-3-36: God gives eternal life to whoever believes in the Son, but whoever rejects the Son will not see life, and God's wrath remains on him.
jhn-4-13-14: Jesus promises that whoever drinks the water He gives will never thirst again; it becomes a spring welling up to eternal life.
jhn-4-23-24: God is spirit and seeks true worshipers who worship Him in spirit and truth.
jhn-5-24: Jesus promises that whoever hears His word and believes the Father who sent Him has eternal life, will not be condemned and has passed from death to life.
jhn-5-28-29: Jesus declares that all in the tombs will hear His voice and come out, those who did good to the resurrection of life and those who did evil to judgment.
jhn-6-35: Jesus says He is the bread of life; whoever comes to Him will not hunger, and whoever believes in Him will never thirst.
jhn-6-37: Jesus promises that all the Father gives Him will come, and whoever comes to Him He will never cast out.
jhn-6-39-40: God's will is that Jesus lose none He has been given; everyone who looks to the Son and believes will have eternal life, and He will raise them on the last day.
jhn-6-47-48: Jesus promises that whoever believes in Him has eternal life, for He is the bread of life.
jhn-6-51: Jesus says He is the living bread from heaven; whoever eats this bread will live forever, and the bread He gives for the world's life is His flesh.
jhn-6-54-56: Jesus promises that whoever eats His flesh and drinks His blood has eternal life, remains in Him, and will be raised on the last day.
jhn-6-63: God's Spirit gives life, and Jesus' words are spirit and life; the flesh profits nothing.
jhn-7-37-38: Jesus invites anyone who thirsts to come to Him and drink, promising that rivers of living water will flow from within whoever believes.
jhn-8-12: Jesus promises that whoever follows Him, the light of the world, will not walk in darkness but have the light of life.
jhn-8-31-32: Jesus tells those who believed Him that if they remain in His word they are truly His disciples, will know the truth, and the truth will set them free.
jhn-8-34-36: Jesus says everyone who sins is a slave to sin, but if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
jhn-8-51: Jesus promises that whoever keeps His word will never see death.
jhn-9-4-5: Jesus must do the works of the One who sent Him while it is day, for while He is in the world He is the light of the world.
jhn-10-9-10: Jesus says He is the door; whoever enters through Him will be saved and find pasture, for He came that they may have life abundantly.
jhn-10-11: Jesus is the good shepherd, who lays down His life for the sheep.
jhn-10-14-15: Jesus is the good shepherd who knows His own and is known by them, as He and the Father know each other, and He lays down His life for the sheep.
jhn-10-27-29: Jesus promises that His sheep, who hear His voice and follow Him, have eternal life and will never perish; no one can snatch them from His hand or the Father's.
jhn-10-30: Jesus declares, "I and the Father are one."
jhn-11-25-26: Jesus says He is the resurrection and the life; whoever believes in Him will live even though he dies, and whoever lives and believes will never die.
jhn-11-40: Jesus reminds Martha that if she believed, she would see God's glory, just before He raised Lazarus.
jhn-12-24-25: Jesus teaches that a grain of wheat must die to bear much fruit; whoever loves his life will lose it, but whoever hates it in this world keeps it for eternal life.
jhn-12-32: Jesus promises that when He is lifted up from the earth, He will draw all people to Himself.
jhn-12-46: Jesus came as light into the world, so that whoever believes in Him will not remain in darkness.
jhn-13-34-35: Jesus gives a new command to love one another as He has loved us, so everyone will know we are His disciples.
jhn-14-1-3: Jesus tells His troubled disciples to trust Him, promising to prepare a place for them in His Father's house and come again to take them to be with Him.
jhn-14-6: Jesus is the way, the truth and the life; no one comes to the Father except through Him.
jhn-14-12-14: Jesus promises that whoever believes in Him will do His works and greater, and whatever they ask in His name He will do, so the Father is glorified.
jhn-14-15-17: Jesus promises those who love Him and keep His commands that the Father will give them the Spirit of truth, another Counselor to be with them forever.
jhn-14-18: Jesus promises, "I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you."
jhn-14-19-20: Jesus promises His disciples that because He lives, they will live too, and they will know that He is in the Father, they in Him and He in them.
jhn-14-21: Jesus promises that whoever has His commands and keeps them loves Him and will be loved by His Father, and Jesus will reveal Himself to him.
jhn-14-23: Jesus promises that whoever loves Him will keep His word, and the Father and Son will love him and make their home with him.
jhn-14-26: Jesus promises that the Father will send the Holy Spirit in His name to teach His disciples all things and remind them of all He said.
jhn-14-27: Jesus gives His disciples His own peace, not as the world gives, so their hearts need not be troubled or afraid.
jhn-15-1-2: God the Father, the vine grower, removes branches in Jesus that bear no fruit and prunes those that bear fruit so they bear more.
jhn-15-4-5: Jesus calls His disciples to remain in Him as branches in the vine; whoever remains in Him bears much fruit, for apart from Him they can do nothing.
jhn-15-7-8: Jesus promises that if His disciples remain in Him and His words remain in them, they may ask whatever they desire and it will be done, bearing fruit that glorifies the Father.
jhn-15-9-11: Jesus loves His disciples as the Father loves Him and calls them to remain in His love by keeping His commands, so His joy may be in them and their joy full.
jhn-15-12-13: Jesus commands His disciples to love one another as He loved them, for no one has greater love than to lay down his life for his friends.
jhn-15-15-16: Jesus calls His disciples friends, chosen and appointed to bear lasting fruit, so that whatever they ask the Father in His name He will give them.
jhn-15-26: Jesus promises to send the Counselor, the Spirit of truth from the Father, who will testify about Him.
jhn-16-7: Jesus tells His disciples it is for their good that He goes away, for then He will send them the Counselor.
jhn-16-13-14: Jesus promises that the Spirit of truth will guide His disciples into all truth, declare what is to come and glorify Him.
jhn-16-20-22: Jesus promises His grieving disciples that their sorrow will turn to joy when He sees them again, and no one will take their joy away.
jhn-16-23-24: Jesus promises that whatever His disciples ask the Father in His name, He will give them; ask and receive, so their joy may be full.
jhn-16-27: God the Father Himself loves those who have loved Jesus and believed He came from God.
jhn-16-33: Jesus tells His disciples they will have trouble in the world, but they can have peace in Him and take heart, for He has overcome the world.
jhn-17-3: Jesus prays that eternal life is to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom He sent.
jhn-17-11: Jesus prays for the Holy Father to keep His disciples through His name, so they may be one as the Father and Son are one.
jhn-17-15-17: Jesus prays not that the Father take His disciples out of the world, but that He keep them from the evil one and sanctify them by His word of truth.
jhn-17-20-23: Jesus prays for all who will believe through the apostles' message, that they may be one in the Father and the Son, so the world may know the Father sent Him and loves them.
jhn-17-24: Jesus prays that those the Father has given Him may be with Him where He is and see His glory.
jhn-17-26: Jesus has made the Father's name known and will continue, so that the Father's love for Him and Jesus Himself may be in His people.
jhn-20-19-21: Jesus, risen, stood among His fearful disciples, showed His wounds and said, "Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, so I send you."
jhn-20-22-23: Jesus breathed on His disciples, saying, "Receive the Holy Spirit," and gave them authority to declare sins forgiven or retained.
jhn-20-27-29: Jesus invited Thomas to touch His wounds and believe, then blessed those who have not seen and yet have believed.
jhn-20-31: God caused this Gospel to be written so readers may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and by believing have life in His name.
act-1-8: Jesus promises His apostles power when the Holy Spirit comes on them, to be His witnesses from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.
act-2-17-18: God promises to pour out His Spirit on all flesh in the last days, sons and daughters, young and old, servants alike, as Peter declares at Pentecost.
act-2-21: God promises that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
act-2-38-39: God promises that those who repent and are baptized in Jesus' name receive forgiveness and the Holy Spirit; the promise is for them, their children and all whom He calls.
act-3-19-21: God calls people to repent and turn back so their sins may be wiped out and times of refreshing come, until He sends Christ to restore all things.
act-4-12: God has given salvation in no one else but Jesus; there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved.
act-10-34-35: God shows no favoritism; in every nation He accepts whoever fears Him and does what is right, as Peter realized in Cornelius' house.
act-10-43: God promises, as all the prophets testify, that everyone who believes in Jesus receives forgiveness of sins through His name.
act-13-38-39: God offers forgiveness of sins through Jesus, and everyone who believes is justified from all that the law of Moses could not justify.
act-16-31: God's promise to the Philippian jailer: believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.
act-18-9-10: Jesus told Paul in a vision at Corinth not to fear but keep speaking, for He was with him, no one would harm him, and He had many people in that city.
act-26-17-18: Jesus promised to rescue Paul and send him to the Gentiles to open their eyes, turning them from darkness to God to receive forgiveness and an inheritance by faith.
rom-1-16-17: God's Good News is His power for salvation to everyone who believes, Jew and Greek alike, revealing His righteousness by faith, for the righteous will live by faith.
rom-3-21-24: God has revealed His righteousness apart from the law through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe; all have sinned, yet are justified freely by His grace through Christ's redemption.
rom-3-25-26: God presented Jesus as an atoning sacrifice through faith in His blood, showing that He is both just and the One who justifies whoever has faith in Jesus.
rom-4-5: God counts as righteous the one who does not rely on works but trusts Him who justifies the ungodly.
rom-4-7-8: God's forgiveness brings true blessing: happy are those whose sins are covered and whom the Lord will not count as guilty.
rom-4-16-17: God made His promise depend on faith and grace, so it is sure to all Abraham's children by faith; He gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not exist.
rom-4-20-22: God's promise held Abraham steady; he did not waver in unbelief but grew strong in faith, fully assured God could do what He promised, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
rom-5-1-2: God gives those justified by faith peace with Him through Jesus Christ, access into His grace, and joy in the hope of His glory.
rom-5-3-5: God uses suffering to produce perseverance, character and hope, a hope that does not disappoint because He has poured His love into our hearts by the Holy Spirit.
rom-5-6-8: God shows His love for us in this: while we were still sinners and powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.
rom-5-9-11: God promises that those now justified by Christ's blood will be saved from wrath through Him; reconciled through His Son's death, they will much more be saved by His life.
rom-5-17: God promises that those who receive His abundant grace and gift of righteousness will reign in life through Jesus Christ.
rom-5-20-21: God's grace overflowed even more where sin increased, so grace reigns through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ.
rom-6-4-5: God raised Christ from the dead so that those united with Him in baptism may walk in new life and share in His resurrection.
rom-6-14: God's grace means sin will not be master over those who are under grace rather than law.
rom-6-23: God's free gift is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord, while the wages of sin is death.
rom-8-1-2: God declares no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus, for the Spirit of life has set them free from the law of sin and death.
rom-8-6: God's Spirit brings life and peace to the mind set on Him, while the mind set on the flesh leads to death.
rom-8-9-11: God's Spirit lives in those who belong to Christ, and the One who raised Jesus from the dead will also give life to their mortal bodies through His Spirit.
rom-8-14-16: God makes all who are led by His Spirit His children; His Spirit of adoption frees them from fear to cry "Abba, Father" and testifies that they are His.
rom-8-17: God makes His children heirs with Christ, sharing His sufferings now so they may share His glory.
rom-8-18: God's coming glory for His people is so great that present sufferings are not worth comparing with it.
rom-8-26-27: God's Spirit helps believers in weakness, interceding for them with groans too deep for words when they do not know how to pray, according to God's will.
rom-8-28: God works all things together for good for those who love Him and are called according to His purpose.
rom-8-29-30: God foreknew and predestined His people to be conformed to His Son's image; those He called He also justified and glorified.
rom-8-31-32: God is for His people; since He did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, He will graciously give us all things with Him.
rom-8-33-34: God justifies His chosen ones, so no charge can stand against them; Christ, who died, rose and intercedes at God's right hand.
rom-8-35-37: God's love in Christ cannot be cut off by trouble, persecution, famine or sword; in all these His people are more than conquerors through Him who loved them.
rom-8-38-39: God's love in Christ Jesus our Lord cannot be separated from His people by death, life, angels, powers, things present or to come, or anything in creation.
rom-10-9-11: God promises that whoever confesses Jesus as Lord and believes in their heart that God raised Him from the dead will be saved and never put to shame.
rom-10-12-13: God is Lord of all, Jew and Greek alike, richly generous to all who call on Him, for everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
rom-11-29: God's gifts and calling are irrevocable.
rom-12-1-2: God's mercies call His people to offer themselves as living sacrifices and be transformed by a renewed mind, so they can discern His good, pleasing and perfect will.
rom-12-12: God's people are called to rejoice in hope, endure in trouble and keep praying faithfully.
rom-12-19: God says vengeance belongs to Him and He will repay, so His people must not take revenge themselves.
rom-15-4: God gave the Scriptures for our instruction, so that through their perseverance and encouragement we might have hope.
rom-15-13: God, the God of hope, is asked to fill believers with all joy and peace in believing, so they overflow with hope by the Holy Spirit's power.
1co-1-8-9: God will keep believers strong to the end, blameless on the day of Christ; He is faithful, having called them into fellowship with His Son.
1co-1-18: God's power is found in the message of the cross for those being saved, though it looks foolish to those perishing.
1co-1-27-29: God chose what the world counts foolish, weak and lowly to shame the wise and strong, so no one can boast before Him.
1co-2-9-10: God has prepared for those who love Him what no eye has seen or ear heard, and He reveals it by His Spirit.
1co-2-12: God has given believers His Spirit, not the world's spirit, so they may understand what He has freely given them.
1co-3-16-17: God's Spirit lives in His people, who together are His holy temple, and He will judge anyone who destroys it.
1co-6-14: God raised the Lord Jesus and will also raise us up by His power.
1co-6-19-20: God's Holy Spirit lives in the believer's body; bought at a price, they belong to God and are called to honor Him with their bodies.
1co-10-13: God is faithful and will not let believers be tempted beyond what they can bear; with the temptation He will provide a way out so they can endure it.
1co-12-4-7: God gives different gifts, services and workings by the same Spirit, Lord and God, and gives each person the Spirit's manifestation for the good of all.
1co-13-4-8: God's way of love is patient and kind, not envious, proud or self-seeking; it bears, believes, hopes and endures all things, and love never fails.
1co-13-12-13: God will one day be known face to face; now we see dimly and know in part, but then we will know fully as we are fully known. Faith, hope and love remain.
1co-15-3-4: God's Good News is that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, was buried and was raised on the third day.
1co-15-20-22: God raised Christ as the firstfruits of those who have died; as all die in Adam, so in Christ all will be made alive.
1co-15-51-52: God will change His people in an instant at the last trumpet: the dead will be raised imperishable, and the living will be transformed.
1co-15-54-57: God will swallow up death in victory when the mortal puts on immortality, and He gives us that victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
1co-15-58: God's people are called to stand firm and give themselves fully to the Lord's work, knowing their labor in the Lord is not in vain.
1co-16-13-14: God's people are called to stay alert, stand firm in the faith, be courageous and strong, and do everything in love.
2co-1-3-4: God, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort, comforts us in all our troubles so we can comfort others with the comfort we receive from Him.
2co-1-5: God's comfort through Christ overflows to His people as fully as they share in Christ's sufferings.
2co-1-20: God's promises, however many, all find their "Yes" in Christ, and through Him we say "Amen" to His glory.
2co-1-21-22: God establishes believers in Christ, anoints and seals them, and gives His Spirit in their hearts as a guarantee of what is to come.
2co-3-17-18: God's Spirit brings freedom, and as believers behold the Lord's glory with unveiled faces they are being transformed into His image from glory to glory.
2co-4-6: God, who commanded light to shine out of darkness, has shone in our hearts to give the knowledge of His glory in the face of Jesus Christ.
2co-4-7-9: God's power at work in fragile clay jars kept Paul and his companions hard pressed but not crushed, persecuted but not forsaken, struck down but not destroyed.
2co-4-16-18: God renews the inner person day by day even as the outer body wastes away, and our light, momentary troubles are producing an eternal weight of glory.
2co-5-1: God has prepared for His people an eternal house in heaven, not made with hands, when their earthly tent is taken down.
2co-5-5: God has prepared us for resurrection life and given His Spirit as a guarantee.
2co-5-7: God's people live by faith, not by sight.
2co-5-17: God makes anyone who is in Christ a new creation; the old has passed away, and the new has come.
2co-5-18-19: God reconciled us to Himself through Christ, not counting people's sins against them, and entrusted to us the message of reconciliation.
2co-5-21: God made Christ, who knew no sin, to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.
2co-6-2: God says He hears and helps in the day of salvation, and now is that acceptable time; now is the day of salvation.
2co-6-16-18: God promises to live among His people and be their God, and calls them to come out and be separate, promising to welcome them as His sons and daughters.
2co-7-6: God, who comforts the downcast, comforted Paul by the arrival of Titus.
2co-9-6-8: God loves a cheerful giver and is able to make all grace abound, so that having enough in all things, givers can abound in every good work.
2co-9-10-11: God, who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food, will supply and increase believers' generosity so their giving overflows in thanksgiving to Him.
2co-12-9-10: God's grace is sufficient, for His power is made perfect in weakness, so Paul boasts in weaknesses, insults and hardships, because when he is weak, then he is strong.
2co-13-11: God's people are urged to rejoice, mend their ways, be of one mind and live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with them.
2co-13-14: God's blessing is prayed over the church: the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.
gal-2-20: God's Son, who loved Paul and gave Himself for him, now lives in him, so the life Paul lives is by faith in Christ.
gal-3-13-14: God redeemed us from the law's curse through Christ, who became a curse for us, so Abraham's blessing might reach the Gentiles and we receive the promised Spirit by faith.
gal-3-26-29: God makes all who have faith in Christ Jesus His children, one in Christ without distinction, and heirs of Abraham's promise.
gal-4-4-7: God sent His Son to redeem those under the law so we might be adopted as His children, and sent His Spirit into our hearts crying "Abba, Father," making us heirs.
gal-5-1: God's people are called to stand firm in the freedom Christ has won for them and not return to a yoke of slavery.
gal-5-13-14: God called His people to freedom, not to indulge the flesh but to serve one another in love, for the whole law is fulfilled in loving your neighbor as yourself.
gal-5-16-18: God's Spirit enables those who walk by Him not to carry out the desires of the flesh.
gal-5-22-23: God's Spirit produces love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.
gal-6-2: God's people fulfill the law of Christ by carrying one another's burdens.
gal-6-7-9: God is not mocked; whoever sows to the Spirit will reap eternal life, so believers should not grow weary in doing good, for they will reap in due season if they do not give up.
eph-1-3-6: God has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing, chose us before creation to be holy, and in love adopted us as His children through Jesus Christ.
eph-1-7-8: God gives redemption through Christ's blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of His grace.
eph-1-13-14: God seals those who believe the Good News with the promised Holy Spirit, a guarantee of their inheritance until He redeems His own possession.
eph-2-4-7: God, rich in mercy and great in love, made us alive with Christ when we were dead in sin and raised us with Him to show His grace in the ages to come.
eph-2-8-10: God saves by grace through faith, as His gift and not by works, and we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works He prepared.
eph-2-13-14: God has brought near through Christ's blood those once far off; Christ is our peace, who broke down the dividing wall between Jew and Gentile.
eph-2-18-19: God gives both Jews and Gentiles access to the Father through Christ by one Spirit, making them fellow citizens and members of His household.
eph-2-20-22: God is building His people on the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus as cornerstone, into a holy temple where He lives by His Spirit.
eph-3-12: God gives us boldness and confident access to Him through faith in Christ.
eph-3-16-19: God is asked to strengthen believers by His Spirit so Christ dwells in their hearts through faith, and rooted in love they know Christ's love that surpasses knowledge.
eph-3-20-21: God is able to do far more abundantly than all we ask or imagine, by His power at work within us; to Him be glory forever.
eph-4-4-6: God has made one body and one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, and is one God and Father of all, over all and in all.
eph-4-22-24: God calls His people to put off the old self, be renewed in mind and put on the new self, created to be like Him in righteousness and holiness.
eph-4-26-27: God's people may be angry but must not sin; they should not let the sun go down on their anger or give the devil a foothold.
eph-4-32: God forgave us in Christ, so His people are to be kind, tenderhearted and forgiving toward one another.
eph-5-1-2: God's beloved children are called to imitate Him and walk in love, as Christ loved us and gave Himself up for us as a fragrant offering.
eph-5-8-9: God has made those once in darkness light in the Lord, so they are to live as children of light, bearing fruit in goodness, righteousness and truth.
eph-5-14: God calls the sleeper to wake and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on him.
eph-6-10-11: God's people are called to be strong in the Lord and put on His full armor, so they can stand against the devil's schemes.
eph-6-13: God's full armor is given so His people can resist in the evil day and, having done everything, still stand.
eph-6-16-17: God gives the shield of faith to extinguish the evil one's fiery arrows, the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is His word.
php-1-6: God, who began a good work in His people, will carry it on to completion until the day of Jesus Christ.
php-1-21: For Paul, to live is Christ and to die is gain.
php-2-13: God works in His people both to will and to act for His good pleasure.
php-3-20-21: God's people are citizens of heaven, awaiting the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform their lowly bodies to be like His glorious body.
php-4-4-5: God's people are called to rejoice in the Lord always and let their gentleness be known to all, for the Lord is near.
php-4-6-7: God's peace, which surpasses all understanding, will guard the hearts and minds of those who bring every request to Him with prayer and thanksgiving instead of anxiety.
php-4-8-9: God's people are called to think on what is true, honorable, pure and lovely and practice what they learned, and the God of peace will be with them.
php-4-11-13: Paul learned contentment in plenty and in need, for he can do all things through Christ who strengthens him.
php-4-19: God will supply every need of the generous Philippian believers according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
col-1-11-12: God is asked to strengthen believers with all power for endurance and patience with joy, giving thanks to the Father who qualified them to share the saints' inheritance in light.
col-1-13-14: God has rescued us from the domain of darkness and brought us into the Kingdom of His beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.
col-1-19-20: God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Christ and through Him to reconcile all things to Himself, making peace through the blood of His cross.
col-1-21-22: God has reconciled those once alienated and hostile through Christ's death, to present them holy, blameless and above reproach before Him.
col-1-27: God made known among the Gentiles the riches of this mystery: Christ in you, the hope of glory.
col-2-6-7: God's people, having received Christ Jesus as Lord, are called to walk in Him, rooted, built up and established in the faith, overflowing with thanksgiving.
col-2-9-10: God's whole fullness dwells bodily in Christ, and in Him believers have been made complete.
col-2-13-14: God made us alive with Christ when we were dead in sin, forgiving all our trespasses and nailing the record of debt against us to the cross.
col-3-1-4: God's people, raised with Christ, are called to set their minds on things above, for their life is hidden with Christ in God, and when He appears they will appear with Him in glory.
col-3-12-15: God's chosen, holy and beloved people are called to put on compassion, kindness, humility and patience, forgive as the Lord forgave them, and let Christ's peace rule their hearts.
col-3-16-17: God's people are called to let Christ's word dwell in them richly and do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to the Father through Him.
1th-1-4-5: God loved and chose the Thessalonian believers, as the Good News came to them in power, in the Holy Spirit and with full conviction.
1th-3-12-13: God is asked to make believers abound in love for one another and for all, so their hearts are established blameless in holiness at Jesus' coming.
1th-4-13-14: God will bring with Jesus those who have died in Him, so believers do not grieve like those without hope.
1th-4-16-18: God promises that the Lord will descend from heaven, the dead in Christ will rise first, and living believers will be caught up with them to be with the Lord forever.
1th-5-9-10: God has not appointed believers to wrath but to obtain salvation through Jesus Christ, who died for them so that, awake or asleep, they will live with Him.
1th-5-16-18: God's will for His people in Christ Jesus is to rejoice always, pray continually and give thanks in all circumstances.
1th-5-23-24: God, the God of peace, is asked to sanctify believers completely and keep them blameless until Christ's coming; He who calls them is faithful and will do it.
2th-1-6-7: God will justly repay those who afflict His people and give relief to the afflicted when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven.
2th-2-13-14: God chose the Thessalonian believers for salvation through the Spirit's sanctifying work and belief in the truth, calling them to share Christ's glory.
2th-2-16-17: God our Father and the Lord Jesus, who loved us and gave eternal comfort and good hope by grace, are asked to comfort believers and strengthen them in every good work and word.
2th-3-3: God the Lord is faithful; He will strengthen believers and guard them from the evil one.
2th-3-16: God, the Lord of peace, is asked to give believers peace at all times and in every way.
1ti-1-14-15: God's grace overflowed to Paul, the worst of sinners, proving the trustworthy saying that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners.
1ti-2-3-6: God our Savior desires all people to be saved and come to know the truth; there is one mediator between God and people, Christ Jesus, who gave Himself as a ransom for all.
1ti-4-8-10: God makes godliness valuable in every way, holding promise for this life and the life to come; our hope is in the living God, Savior of all, especially of those who believe.
1ti-6-6-8: God's people find great gain in godliness with contentment, for we brought nothing into the world and can take nothing out; with food and clothing we will be content.
1ti-6-12: God calls His people to fight the good fight of faith and take hold of the eternal life to which they were called.
1ti-6-17-19: God, who richly provides everything to enjoy, is where the wealthy must set their hope rather than uncertain riches, being generous and rich in good works.
2ti-1-7: God did not give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love and self-control.
2ti-1-9-10: God saved us and called us by His own purpose and grace given in Christ before time began, now revealed in Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light.
2ti-1-12: God is able to guard what Paul has entrusted to Him until that day, so he is not ashamed of his suffering.
2ti-2-11-13: God's trustworthy saying: if we died with Christ we will live with Him; if we endure we will reign; if we deny Him He will deny us; if we are faithless He remains faithful.
2ti-2-19: God's firm foundation stands: the Lord knows those who are His, and everyone who names Him must turn from wickedness.
2ti-3-15-17: God breathed out all Scripture, which makes us wise for salvation through faith in Christ and equips His people for every good work.
2ti-4-7-8: God, the righteous Judge, will give Paul the crown of righteousness, and not only him but all who have loved His appearing.
2ti-4-17-18: God stood by Paul and strengthened him when everyone deserted him, and Paul trusts the Lord to rescue him from every evil deed and bring him safely to His heavenly Kingdom.
tit-1-1-2: God, who cannot lie, promised eternal life before time began.
tit-2-11-14: God's grace has appeared, bringing salvation and training us to live godly lives as we await the appearing of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, who gave Himself to redeem us.
tit-3-4-7: God our Savior saved us not by our works but by His mercy, through the washing of rebirth and renewal of the Holy Spirit, so that justified by grace we become heirs of eternal life.
phm-1-4-7: God is thanked for Philemon's love and faith, and Paul prays that his shared faith becomes effective, for he has refreshed the hearts of the saints.
heb-1-3: The writer of Hebrews describes the Son as the radiance of God's glory and the exact representation of his being. He sustains everything by his word, and after cleansing sins he sat down at God's right hand.
heb-2-14-15: The writer explains that Jesus became fully human so that through his death he could break the devil's power over death. He frees those who lived their whole lives enslaved by the fear of death.
heb-2-17-18: The writer explains that Jesus became like us in every way so he could be a merciful and faithful high priest, making atonement for sins. Because he suffered when tempted, he can help those being tempted.
heb-3-6: The writer contrasts Moses, a servant in God's house, with Christ, a faithful Son over it. Believers are his house, provided they keep holding firmly to their confidence and hope.
heb-4-9-11: The writer says that a Sabbath rest still awaits God's people, a rest Joshua never fully gave Israel. Those who enter it rest from their labours, so readers should make every effort to enter, and not fall through unbelief.
heb-4-12-13: The writer warns that God's word is living and active, sharper than any sword, exposing our deepest thoughts and motives. Nothing is hidden from God, to whom we must give account.
heb-4-14-16: The writer urges readers to hold firmly to their faith, because Jesus is a great high priest who understands our weaknesses and was tempted yet never sinned. So we can approach God's throne boldly for mercy and help.
heb-6-10: After a stern warning, the writer reassures readers that God is fair and will not forget the work they have done and the love they have shown by serving fellow believers.
heb-6-17-19: The writer explains that God confirmed his promise to Abraham with an oath, so his heirs would know his purpose cannot change. Since God cannot lie, this hope is a firm, secure anchor for the soul.
heb-7-24-25: The writer explains that unlike earlier priests who died, Jesus lives for ever, so his priesthood is permanent. He can save completely those who come to God through him, because he always lives to intercede for them.
heb-8-10-12: God promised Israel through Jeremiah a new covenant: he would write his laws on their hearts, be their God and forgive their sins completely. Hebrews shows that Christ has brought this covenant into effect.
heb-9-12: The writer contrasts the yearly animal sacrifices of the high priest with Christ, who entered God's presence once for all with his own blood, securing a redemption that lasts for ever.
heb-9-14: The writer reasons that if animal blood could make people outwardly clean, Christ's blood, offered to God through the eternal Spirit, can do far more: cleanse our consciences so we can serve the living God.
heb-9-27-28: The writer explains that people die once and then face judgment. In the same way Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many, and he will return, not to deal with sin, but to save those waiting for him.
heb-10-14: The writer explains that by his single sacrifice Christ has made perfect for ever those who are being made holy. Nothing needs to be added to it.
heb-10-16-17: Hebrews repeats God's new covenant promise first given through Jeremiah: he will put his laws in his people's hearts and minds and will never again remember their sins. So no further sacrifice is needed.
heb-10-19-22: The writer tells believers that Jesus' blood has opened a new and living way into God's presence. With Jesus as their great priest, they should draw near to God with sincere hearts and full assurance of faith.
heb-10-23: The writer urges readers under pressure to keep holding to the hope they profess without wavering, because God, who made the promise, is faithful.
heb-10-35-36: Remembering their earlier courage under persecution, the writer urges readers not to throw away their confidence, which will be richly rewarded. They need endurance, so that after doing God's will they receive what he promised.
heb-11-1: The writer defines faith as being sure of what we hope for and convinced of realities we cannot see, introducing a long list of Old Testament examples.
heb-11-6: The writer says it is impossible to please God without faith. Anyone who comes to him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who earnestly seek him.
heb-11-11: The writer recalls how Sarah, though long past childbearing age, received power to conceive, because she considered God faithful to keep his promise.
heb-12-1-2: Surrounded by the faithful witnesses of the past, believers should throw off every hindrance and sin and run their race with endurance. They are to fix their eyes on Jesus, who endured the cross.
heb-12-5-6: The writer reminds suffering believers of Proverbs' advice not to despise the Lord's discipline or lose heart. God disciplines those he loves, as a father corrects a child he accepts.
heb-12-10-11: The writer compares human fathers, who disciplined imperfectly for a short time, with God, who disciplines for our good so we can share his holiness. Discipline hurts at the time, but later it produces peace and righteousness.
heb-12-28: The writer says that while the created world will be shaken, believers are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken. So they should be thankful and worship God with reverence and awe.
heb-13-5-6: The writer urges readers not to love money but to be content, quoting God's pledge never to leave or abandon his people. Because of this, believers can say with confidence that the Lord helps them and they need not fear.
heb-13-8: Urging readers to remember faithful leaders and avoid strange teachings, the writer declares that Jesus Christ does not change: he is the same yesterday, today and for ever.
heb-13-20-21: The writer closes with a blessing: may the God of peace, who raised Jesus, the great Shepherd, through the blood of the eternal covenant, equip readers with everything good to do his will, working in them what pleases him.
jas-1-2-4: James tells believers to treat trials as a reason for joy, not because suffering is good, but because testing their faith builds endurance. Endurance, allowed to finish its work, makes them mature and complete.
jas-1-5-6: James tells anyone lacking wisdom, especially in trials, to ask God, who gives generously to all without scolding. They should ask trusting him, not torn by doubt like a wave tossed by the wind.
jas-1-12: James says people who endure testing are blessed. Once they have stood the test, they will receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love him.
jas-1-17-18: James insists that God does not tempt anyone; every good and perfect gift comes from him, the unchanging Father of the heavenly lights. By his own choice he gave believers new birth through the word of truth.
